Designing nanocomposites or core-shell structures with magnetocaloric materials can improve the magnetocaloric effect by increasing the surface area, reducing the thermal conductivity, and modifying the magnetic anisotropy, with key parameters including particle size (e.g., 10-50 nm), shell thickness (e.g., 1-5 nm), and interface properties (e.g., exchange bias, spin polarization)

Introduction of transition metals like Mn, Fe, or Co into the crystal structure of magnetocaloric materials can enhance the magnetic moment and improve the magnetocaloric effect by modifying the magnetic exchange interactions and anisotropy, with key parameters including doping concentration (e.g., 5-10%) and temperature range (e.g., 250-300 K)
